input.title: feat: restore authored creator category tabs
input.body:
## Summary

Replace the creator's generic category buttons with the authored native/mock tabs.

```text
avatar → Body / Primary / Secondary / Passive
enemy  → Body / Weapons / Behavior
inactive ↔ rollover; selected retains rollover paint
click selected → keep chosen part
```

Use the existing numeric registrations and per-pack artwork cache; the editor still owns category, chosen part and pending placement. This is the next small slice of the original recreation backlog, based on merged #59.

## Evidence

- **Before:** A generic flex column paints text buttons and reselecting the active category resets the chosen part.
  **After:** Source-sized and positioned tab artwork selects the proper category; activating the selected tab preserves the chosen part, matching the source's removed click listener.
- Source: TankCreatorScreen `_-bl`, `LibraryTabRollOver`, `_-Tx`, `_-ER` and mode-specific tab removals. Browser geometry uses fixed source coordinates; existing importer/cache evidence covers the numerical facts and clamped inactive frames.
- Formatting, TypeScript, 496 rule tests (6,102 assertions) and production build pass. All eight affected browser cases pass across native/mock controls, affordability, final tab and in-game editor runs, without skips.
- New checks verify rollover paint changes/restoration, selected paint retention, selected-tab no-op, avatar/enemy categories, preview choice, Enter/Space, creator remount and in-game tab activation/cancellation. All four native/mock avatar/enemy captures inspected.
- React keeps stable category keys and derives paint directly from props/hover, with no effects or global listeners. Decorative art is hidden from assistive technology; buttons retain names and pressed state.
- Backdrop/rows/scrollbar, full-size preview and complete original-screen timing remain pending. Mock font contours/baselines and rectangular hit targets remain explicit boundaries. No original media or generated metadata changed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores the prior category column.

**Blast Radius:** editor

Shared tabs affect standalone, library and in-game creator entry; all three paths are covered.

title: use client
description: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client.
---

The `'use client'` directive declares an entry point for the components to be rendered on the **client side** and should be used when creating interactive user interfaces (UI) that require client-side JavaScript capabilities, such as state management, event handling, and access to browser APIs. This is a React feature.

> **Good to know:**
>
> You do not need to add the `'use client'` directive to every file that contains Client Components. You only need to add it to the files whose components you want to render directly within Server Components. The `'use client'` directive defines the [server and client boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary), and the components exported from such a file serve as entry points to the client.

## Usage

To declare an entry point for the Client Components, add the `'use client'` directive **at the top of the file**, before any imports. The directive applies to the entire module and cannot be placed inside a component or function:
